answer: The sable multiplier is published, charged in lantern, and harbor lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3631 identities would post 1490 proofs and burn roughly 45 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
